data.qǝʍᴉʍǝp#qǝʍᴉʍǝp:
Stage manager based in Rennes, France. I work in live performance while developing open source tools at the intersection of digital and stage production.
My projects revolve around spatial audio, control protocols (OSC, Ember+, MIDI/XCTL) and practical utilities for production.
What I do Live performance — Stage manager by training and practice, with a technical approach to the stage and production workflow Open source development — Active contributor on GitHub since 2013, projects in JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Python and C Technical integration — Specialised in interfacing stage and audiovisual equipment via open protocols Links GitHub — github.com/dewiweb Initiated projects Contributions

data: These are the repositories I created and maintain. They mainly cover spatial audio, stage control protocols and utility tools.
Projects around 3D audio, immersive sound and tools for driving spatialisation systems.

data.features#Features: Automatic stream discovery via SAP/mDNS Manual stream entry by pasting SDP Direct Dante device queries via ARC (name, model, TX/RX channels) 16-slot monitoring wall with drag-and-drop Real-time dBFS metering with peak hold Listen to any stream with channel selection PTP tracking (IEEE 1588 grandmaster, per-stream lock status) UI in 8 languages Windows, macOS, Linux
data.overview#Overview: Cross-platform desktop application for visualizing and monitoring audio-over-IP streams: AES67, ST2110-30, RAVENNA and Dante. Automatic stream discovery on the network, playback, level metering and PTP tracking.
data.tech-stack#Tech stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + TailwindCSS, Electron desktop shell, audio via Audify (RtAudio bindings).

data.features#Features: Linux kernel module (Loadable Kernel Module) RAVENNA/AES67 audio transport over IP Native ALSA integration Compatible with Merging Technologies equipment and other AES67 devices
data.links#Links: GitHub repository Original source (Merging Technologies) Language: C Topics: aes67 alsa driver linux
data.overview#Overview:
Clone of the ALSA RAVENNA/AES67 driver originally provided by Merging Technologies. This Linux kernel module (LKM) enables the RAVENNA network audio transport protocol (compatible with AES67) within the ALSA subsystem on Linux.
RAVENNA/AES67 is a professional audio-over-IP transport standard used in studios, concert halls and broadcast installations.

data.features#Features: Control Holophonix sources from Chataigne Bidirectional OSC communication Integration into show control workflows
data.overview#Overview: A Python module integrating the Holophonix spatial audio processor into Chataigne — a modular software for arts and technology. Drives spatial sound sources from Chataigne’s interface via OSC.

data.features#Features: Import Holophonix projects (.hol, .zip) Track discovery via OSC /dump request Real-time animation (loop / ping-pong / once modes) Simultaneous animations — each track runs independently Cue list — trigger, stop and blend animations on demand Motion models (extensible JSON): circular, linear, figure-8, spiral, pendulum, random walk OSC output /track/{id}/xyz in real time during playback
data.overview#Overview: Port of holophonix-animator as a native Blender addon: create and play motion animations for Holophonix spatial audio tracks directly inside Blender’s 3D View. Complements holophonix_blender_addon, which focuses on project management.
data.requirements#Requirements: Blender 4.2+ (tested on 5.0) OSC libs bundled — no external install needed

data.features#Features: Create movement behaviours (circles, lines, free trajectories) Manage multiple tracks simultaneously OSC synchronisation with Holophonix Desktop GUI (Electron/Node.js)
data.overview#Overview:
Desktop application for creating and managing movement animations for spatial audio tracks on the Holophonix processor.
It communicates with Holophonix via the OSC protocol and lets you define trajectories and dynamic behaviours for sound sources in 3D space.

data.features#Features: Control Holophonix spatial audio sources from Chataigne Read/write parameters via OSC Integration into complex show control workflows Compatible with recent Holophonix versions
data.overview#Overview: A Chataigne module dedicated to the Holophonix spatial audio processor. Natively integrates Holophonix into Chataigne to drive sound sources, read states and automate behaviours in a show control context.

data.features#Features: Dante leader (PTPv1) — who sends Sync, sync interval, jitter (mean/min/max/σ), leader change history AES67 grandmaster (PTPv2) — clock identity, priorities, clock class, steps removed, announce timing Per-source stats — message types, rates, sequence gaps/dupes, silence detection, non-standard PTP domains Malformed packets — unparsable datagrams logged with source IP and full hexdump Evidence logs — chronological JSONL journal + optional full packet capture Network-agnostic — no hard-coded addresses; friendly device names via devices.json, reverse DNS and the IEEE OUI database
data.links#Links: GitHub repository Language: Python (Qt / PySide6) The UI is currently in French — i18n contributions are welcome.
data.overview#Overview:
Desktop tool (Qt / PySide6) for passively listening to PTP clock traffic on a production audio-over-IP network — to detect problems and record evidence for vendor support cases.
100% passive: it joins the standard PTP multicast group 224.0.1.129 (UDP 319/320) and listens. It never sends a single PTP packet and cannot disturb the clock election or timing of the network.

data.features#Features: Read 6DoF data (X/Y/Z translation + rotation) from the SpaceMouse Convert and send data as OSC messages Configurable mappings (axes, OSC addresses, value ranges) Low latency for real-time control
data.links#Links: GitHub repository Language: JavaScript Licence: MIT Topics: 3dconnexion 6dof osc spacemouse spatial-audio
data.overview#Overview:
Bridge between the 3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Compact and the OSC (Open Sound Control) protocol. Lets you use the 6DoF (6 degrees of freedom) controller to drive sound sources in 3D space in real time.
Particularly well suited to controlling spatialisation systems such as Holophonix, Max/MSP or SuperCollider.

data.features#Features: GUI for defining movement trajectories Real-time OSC output Modern TypeScript architecture Compatible with OSC systems (Holophonix, Max/MSP, etc.)
data.overview#Overview:
Full rewrite of the Trajectoires application, a web/mobile interface for controlling sound spatialisation via OSC. This modernised version is developed in TypeScript with a revised architecture.
Trajectoires lets you draw and animate trajectories for sound sources in space, then send them in real time to a spatialisation system.

data.features#Features: Node.js backend + HLS streaming (HTTPS/TLS) AES67/RTP multicast input (L24/48 kHz) from QSYS/Dante consoles Listener PWA + control-room admin UI Security (JWT, CSP, bcrypt), Docker/Portainer deployment CI/CD GitHub Actions → GHCR (amd64 + arm64)
data.overview#Overview:
DIY multichannel audio distribution system for theatres, conference halls and cinemas (~450 seats), designed for audio description, hearing assistance (hard-of-hearing audiences) and multilingual simultaneous interpretation.
Audio is received via AES67/RTP from the mixing console, encoded to HLS by FFmpeg and served to audience smartphones through a PWA — no app to install.
data.status#Status: ✅ Operational — real-world testing (450 clients) in progress; WebRTC (< 200 ms) planned to reduce latency.

data.features#Features: Displays above all windows (OSD overlay) Click-through: the mouse passes through the clock Draggable, system tray icon Full settings: font, size, colors, opacity, strftime format, position (9 zones), screen selection Real-time preview, persistent configuration Works with Cinnamon, GNOME, KDE, XFCE, MATE, i3, Openbox…
data.overview#Overview: Always-on-top OSD clock for Linux X11 — the control-room tool that keeps the time visible on any workstation, above every window. Configurable, lightweight, universal.

data.common-features#Common features: Date, duration, venue, price, audience and accessibility (LSF, audio description, surtitling) extracted from OpenAgenda data Native-resolution images, FTP/SMB/local sync Slide of the day, scheduler, gallery
data.links#Links: nextevents · nextevents-desktop · nextevents-php See also openagenda-slides — the generalized version for any public OpenAgenda agenda
data.overview#Overview:
A suite of tools generating slideshows of Les Champs Libres events (Rennes, France) from OpenAgenda data — UHD slides ready for OBS, digital signage and kiosks.
Three variants depending on the infrastructure:
nextevents — Debian/Docker server: scrapes leschampslibres.fr + OpenAgenda, renders UHD 3840×2160 PNGs matching the venue’s visual identity (Oldschool Grotesk typeface, per-event pastel background), web UI with gallery and auto-refresh nextevents-desktop — rewritten as a portable PySide6/Qt app (Windows zip, Linux AppImage): same slide generation plus a native fullscreen player, no Docker or server needed nextevents-php — lightweight PHP port for kiosks: self-contained HTML slides (fonts/images in base64), no PNG generation, no dependencies — the kiosk browser does the rendering

data.features#Features: Portable Qt desktop app for Windows and Linux (AppImage) — no install One polished slide per event Landscape, portrait and printable formats Binaries available in GitHub Releases
data.overview#Overview:
Generalization of nextevents: turns any public OpenAgenda agenda into screen slideshows — one slide per event (image, date, venue, price, audience…) for TVs, kiosks and digital signage, in 16:9, 9:16 portrait or printable A4.
No technical skills required: download, enter your agenda, click Generate.

data.features#Features: Autoplay on boot Supports: video, PDF, PowerPoint (converted), image slideshows Load from USB stick or local storage Chromium in kiosk mode (full-screen, no UI) Simple configuration
data.overview#Overview:
A plug-and-play solution to turn any Raspberry Pi into a full-screen media kiosk player. Automatically plays videos, PowerPoint presentations, PDFs and image slideshows from a USB stick or local storage — all rendered via Chromium.
Ideal for installations, exhibitions, digital signage or any stage use case requiring automatic media playback.
data.requirements#Requirements: Raspberry Pi (any recent generation) Raspberry Pi OS Chromium (included by default on Raspberry Pi OS)

data.features#Features: Vue 3 web UI over HTTPS — simple mode (operator) and expert mode (tech) Secured Go API (HttpOnly sessions, argon2id passwords, operator/tech roles) Go network orchestrator — automatic generation of 802.1q VLANs, bridges, firewall, DHCP, QoS/NIC tuning and PTP Per-service configuration — each protocol (Dante, NDI, AES67/RAVENNA, ST 2110, Art-Net, sACN, PTP, AVB, NMOS, MA-Net…) gets its own VLAN, DSCP, priority and MTU Configurable AV trunk and dedicated ST 2110 interface with jumbo frames (MTU 9000) NTP server with DHCP option 42 per VLAN, mDNS reflector across AV VLANs Monitoring: CPU/memory/services, alerts, filterable logs, SNMP v2c/v3 agent, Prometheus metrics
data.links#Links: GitHub repository Languages: Go, Vue 3, OpenWrt
data.overview#Overview: Router OS designed for live performance environments, based on OpenWrt. StageNeth separates audio/video/lighting (AV) streams from the management network and provides the services stage equipment relies on: DHCP, NTP, mDNS, SNMP and PTP.
data.status#Status: 🚧 Active development (v0.2.0-beta) — validate on the bench before any production use.

data: Projects around protocols used to interconnect stage equipment: OSC, Ember+, XCTL.

data.features#Features: Ember+ client (consumer) implementation Ember+ server (provider) implementation Written in Rust (performance, memory safety)
data.overview#Overview:
A Rust implementation of the Ember+ protocol, covering both the client (consumer) and server (provider) roles.
Ember+ is a control protocol used in the broadcast and audiovisual industry for communication between equipment (mixers, routers, monitoring systems…).
data.why-rust#Why Rust?: Rust provides excellent memory-safety guarantees and performance for a low-level protocol like Ember+, which requires reliable, low-latency communication.

data.features#Features: Bidirectional Ember+ ↔ OSC translation Adapted to Lawo MCx console specifics Interfacing with show control systems via OSC
data.overview#Overview: A bridge between the Ember+ and OSC protocols, specifically designed for Lawo MCx consoles. Allows controlling and monitoring an MCx console from any OSC environment (Chataigne, Max/MSP, QLab, etc.).

data.architecture#Architecture:
Monorepo with two packages:
Backend (Node.js / TypeScript) — Ember+ engine, OSC engine, REST API, WebSocket Frontend (React / Vite) — web UI for configuration and monitoring
data.features#Features: Bidirectional Ember+ ↔ OSC bridge in real time Web UI for device configuration (IP, ports, mappings) Built-in Ember+ tree explorer Session system — save and reload connection mappings Full REST API + WebSocket for third-party integrations Matrix view for Ember+ routers Docker deployment (one-liner, Compose, Portainer) Compatible with LAWO MC², Riedel MediorNet, and any Ember+ device
data.overview#Overview:
MCxOSCnext is a full rewrite of MCxOSC — evolved from a desktop Electron app into a web microservice deployable via Docker. It bridges Ember+ devices (LAWO MC² consoles, Riedel MediorNet matrices…) with OSC control systems (QLab, Chataigne, Max/MSP…).
┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ │ Ember+ │◄───►│ MCxOSC Bridge │◄───►│ OSC │ │ (LAWO MC²) │ TCP │ Backend :3000 UI :80 │ UDP │ (QLab...) │ └─────────────┘ └──────────────────────────┘ └─────────────┘

data.contents#Contents: XCTL message structure Control mapping (faders, encoders, buttons, LEDs, displays) JavaScript implementation examples Comparison with HUI and Mackie Control protocols
data.links#Links: GitHub repository Online documentation Language: JavaScript Licence: GPL-3.0
data.overview#Overview:
Reference documentation for the XCTL protocol used by Behringer X-Touch mixing consoles (and compatible surfaces). This MIDI-extended protocol enables bidirectional communication between the control surface and a DAW or custom control system.
This repository collects information gathered through reverse engineering and community documentation — officially undocumented by Behringer.
